text:
ConocoPhillips rose slightly today as oil prices jumped 3% to above $90 a barrel following U.S. military strikes on Iranian targets—the first such action in weeks. Since the stock has fallen roughly 4% over the past week despite this morning's oil price spike, the small gain today suggests the market is cautiously testing whether geopolitical tension will sustain higher crude prices, which directly improves the economics of oil producers like ConocoPhillips.

The broader backdrop matters: tensions between the U.S. and Iran, plus Russian threats to strike Ukrainian energy infrastructure, have created genuine supply-risk premiums in global oil markets (world crude is trading $88.24 versus U.S. crude at $83.90). These geopolitical flare-ups tend to be volatile and unpredictable, which may explain why the stock has been drifting lower even as headline risks have mounted—investors are uncertain whether the price bump will last or fade as quickly as the last crisis.
